newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish O/N depos rise, zloty edges up vs basket.
newsitem.headline: Polish O/N depos rise, zloty edges up vs basket.

text.p: Polish overnight deposit rates stabilised around 19 percent in balanced trade on Monday after severe overliquidity kept rates at lower levels for most of August, dealers said.

"The market stabilised today -- the first day of the September reserve period -- which was apparent by tighter spreads and interest from both buyers and sellers," said Marek Wieczorkiewicz from PKO BP.
O/N rates were at 18.52/19.10 percent, against 18.0/19.0 at 0640 GMT and Friday's 7.0/11.0 percent and tomorrow/next rates at 18.40/19.05 percent, against Friday's 18.2/18.80 percent.
Dealers said the central bank would likely continue to lenghten the investment horizon for its drainages and offer NBP-bills instead of a reverse repo operation on Tuesday.
"The central bank will probably try to place its NBP-bills tomorrow to lenghten the average term of auction deposits," PKO BP's Wieczorkiewicz said.
Dealers said trade of T-bill repos livened up on Monday with the market's focus on seven to 14 day transactions done around 18.9/19.0 percent.
Minimum prices of most T-bills rose at today's 700 million zloty primary auction on total demand of 1.92 billion zlotys.
The average yield of 52-week paper fell 0.07 point to 19.39 percent but the minimum price remained flat at 83.53.

The Polish zloty recouped slight intraday losses and closed stronger at 1.78/1.76 percent from the trading band centre against Friday's close at 1.75/1.66 percent as the supply of currencies on the market increased in late trade, dealers said.

They were mixed about the origin of additional currencies after last week's light currency buying sentiment, but some said it came from small-scale foreign investor entry in Polish T-bills at today's auction.
The zloty closed the session at 2.7433/38 to the dollar, flaat from 2.7420/40 on Friday and at 1.8491/97 to the mark, also flat from Friday's 1.8490/05.
